title: Restructure prose without changing its meaning
text: When a word-for-word replacement is ungrammatical, unclear, or inaccurate, rewrite the sentence around its intended technical meaning. Preserve the actors, actions, objects, negation, modality, conditions, sequence, quantities, limits, and technical relationships. Use a different construction, or reorganize sentences, lists, or tables, only if the same information and dependencies remain clear. Check related text, cross-references, and independently retrieved fragments for unintended effects. Preserve quotations and machine-significant literals exactly. If the source meaning is unclear or incomplete, obtain clarification from an authoritative source or subject-matter expert before proposing a definitive rewrite; do not invent facts to make the sentence fluent.
exceptions: Brevity, lexical preferences, and local length limits do not authorize dropping a prerequisite, qualification, required action, or safety and security constraint. Remove only information established as unnecessary for the intended communication, not information that is merely difficult to express.
A vocabulary substitution is not proof of grammatical or technical equivalence. Check the applicable lexical meaning, function, and forms independently; this pilot supplies no controlled vocabulary.

Do not rewrite inside an externally controlled literal. Add an explanation outside it when needed. If a governing requirement conflicts with preserving meaning or exact syntax, stop and escalate to the responsible editor or technical owner.
Supporting IDs are planning references only; they neither establish canonical relations nor transfer the source facets recorded here.
